metadata.title: Formalizing Axiomatic Theories of Truth (Lean blueprint)

nodes.name: De Bruijn indices
nodes.statement: To allow for efficient automatic formulas manipulation, variables bound by a quantifier are associated with De Bruijn \cite{bruijn:1972} indices in \texttt{mathlib}'s implementation of first-order formulas. These indices are natural numbers that correspond to the level-distance between the variable and the quantifier that binds it.
differentia: correspond to the level-distance between the variable and the quantifier that binds it

nodes.name: Running example formula
nodes.statement: \forall x (\forall y (P(y) \to R(f(x))) \to (R(z) \to P(a))),

nodes.name: Running example formula in De Bruijn notation
nodes.statement: \forall (\forall (P(0) \to R(f(1))) \to (R(1) \to P(a))).
nodes.label: fml:db

nodes.name: Running example formula and its De Bruijn form
nodes.statement:
Take as an example the regular first-order formula 
\begin{align}
    \forall x (\forall y (P(y) \to R(f(x))) \to (R(z) \to P(a))),
\end{align} where $x, y$ are bound variables, $z$ is a free variables, $P$ and $R$ are predicates and $a$ is a constant.
In De Bruijn notation this formula is expressed by
\begin{align} \forall (\forall (P(0) \to R(f(1))) \to (R(1) \to P(a))).
\end{align}
Troughout this documentation we will use this formula as illustration to the concepts introduced.
nodes.statement_short: Example formula with bound, free variables, predicates and a constant, and its De Bruijn rewriting; used throughout.

nodes.name: First-order Language
nodes.statement: A language is a structure $\langle(F_i)_{i\in \mathbb{N}}, (R_i)_{i\in \mathbb{N}})\rangle$, where $F_i$ is a set of $i$-ary function symbols and $R_i$ a set of $i$-ary predicate symbols.
nodes.statement_short: A language is a pair of arity-indexed families of function symbols and predicate symbols.
nodes.label: def:FO-Language

nodes.name: Constants as 0-ary functions
nodes.statement: Observe, however, that constants can be modeled as $0$-ary functions, so this definition of a language does not limit expressive power.

nodes.name: Language of the running example
nodes.statement: So, the language in which our formula \ref{fml:db} is stated can be defined as $\mathcal{L}_{ex} = \langle (F_{ex,i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}, (R_{ex,i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \rangle$, where $(F_{ex,i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ is defined by $F_{ex,0} = \{a\}$ and $F_{ex,1} = \{f\}$ and $(R_{ex,i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ is defined by $R_{ex,1} = \{P, R\}$.
nodes.statement_short: The language $\mathcal{L}_{ex}$ of the running example: constant $a$, unary function $f$, unary predicates $P,R$.

nodes.name: First-order Term
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L} = \langle F, R \rangle$ be a first-order language and $\alpha$ a set used to index free variables. Then the set of terms with respect to $\mathcal{L}$ and $\alpha$ denoted $\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},\alpha)$ is the smallest set such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\alpha \subseteq \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},\alpha)$ and \item for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$, if $f \in F(i)$ and $x_1,...,x_i \in \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},\alpha)$, then $f(x_1,...,x_i) \in \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},\alpha)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Terms over a language and variable index set: smallest set containing variables and closed under applying function symbols.
nodes.label: def:FO-Term

nodes.name: Disjoint Union
nodes.statement: The disjoint union, denoted $\sqcup$, of two sets $A$ and $B$ is defined as $A \sqcup B = \{(a,k) | (a \in A \wedge k = l) \vee (a \in B \wedge k = r)\}$.
nodes.label: def:Disjoint-Union

nodes.name: Notation #a and &a for disjoint-union elements
nodes.statement: We shall from here on out refer to $(a,l)$ from a disjoint union of sets by $\#a$ and $(a,r)$ by $\&a$.

nodes.name: First-order BoundedFormula
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L} = \langle (F_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}, (R_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \rangle$ be a first-order language, $\alpha$ a set indexing free variables, $n$ the intended number of variables bound by a quantifier and $\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L}, \alpha \sqcup \{1,...,n\})$ the set of terms. Then, the set of bounded formulas with respect to these variables $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n)$ is the smallest set such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\bot \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n)$, \item if $t_1,t_2 \in \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L}, \alpha \sqcup \{0,...,n-1\})$, then $t_1 = t_2 \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n)$, \item for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$, if $P \in R_i$ and $t_1,...,t_i \in \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L}, \alpha \sqcup \{0,...,n-1\})$, then $P(t_1,...,t_i) \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n)$, \item if $f_1,f_2 \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n)$, then $(f_1 \supset f_2) \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n)$ and \item if $f \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n+1)$, then $\forall f \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Bounded formulas with free variables from $\alpha$ and $n$ bound-variable slots: built from $\bot$, equality, relations, implication and $\forall$.
nodes.label: def:FO-BoundedFormula

nodes.name: Difference from classical De Bruijn notation
nodes.statement: Notice that these definitions differ from classical De Bruijn \cite{bruijn:1972} notation in the way variable binding is organized. Firstly, the disjoint union operator in Definition \ref{def:FO-BoundedFormula}'s clauses 2 and 3 guarantees that free variables and variables bound by a quantifier can only be constructed from different sets, whereas in classical De Bruijn all variables are indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. The reason for such an implementation is that now we can distinguish free variables from bound variables. This makes it straightforward to keep track in the recursive cases of what the first free variable is. This is useful for substitution, which will be made clearer shortly. Furthermore, free variables can now come from any set, rather than $\mathbb{N}$, as they are not bound and hence do not have to indicate at what level they are bound.
nodes.statement_short: Separating free and bound variables via disjoint union lets free variables come from any set and simplifies substitution.

nodes.name: Running example in BoundedFormula notation
nodes.statement: These two notational nuances require a slight rewrite of our example formula \ref{fml:db} to $\forall (\forall(P(\&0) \rightarrow R(f(\&1))) \to (R(\#x_0) \to P(a)))$, where $x_0$ is some element from the relevant type $\alpha$ for indexing free variables.

nodes.name: Substitution in Terms
nodes.statement: For some language $\mathcal{L}$, we define the substitution function of terms in terms $/(t) : \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},(\mathbb{N} \sqcup \{1,...,n\}) \to \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},(\mathbb{N} \sqcup \{1,...,n\}) \to \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},(\mathbb{N} \sqcup \{1,...,n\})$ recursively by \begin{enumerate} \item $t/(a) = \begin{cases} t & \text{if } a = \#0 \\ t & \text{otherwise } \end{cases}$ and \item $f(t_1,...,t_n)/(a) = f(t_1/(a),...,t_n/(a))$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Recursive substitution of a term for the first free variable in terms.
nodes.label: def:Term-Substitution

nodes.name: Substitution in BoundedFormulas
nodes.statement: For some language $\mathcal{L}$ and a natural number $n$, we define the substitution function of terms in BoundedFormulas $/(t) : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N},n) \to \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},(\mathbb{N} \sqcup \{1,...,n\}) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N},n)$ recursively by \begin{enumerate} \item $\bot/(t) = \bot$; \item $(t_1 = t_2)/(t) = (t_1/(t) = t_2/(t))$; \item $R(t_1,...,t_n) = R(t_1/(t),...,t_n/(t))$; \item $(\varphi \supset \psi)/(t) = (\varphi/(t) \supset \psi/(t))$ and \item $(\forall \varphi)/(t) = \forall (\varphi/(t))$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Recursive substitution of a term for free variables in bounded formulas, commuting with all connectives and $\forall$.
nodes.label: def:BF-Substitution

nodes.name: Free-variable substitution avoids variable capture
nodes.statement: Note that especially the substitution in clause 5 is different from the standard De Bruijn substitution. See From \cite{from:2021} for an exposition on a first-order De Bruijn-style substitution implementation. Consider a formula in standard De Bruijn notation $\varphi = \forall P(0,1)$. If we would now want to substitute the term $t$ for the first free variable in $\varphi$ using our substitution function, we would write $\forall P(0,1)/(t) = \forall (P(0,1)/(t))$, but note here that substituting the first free variable in $P(0,1)$ does not target the variable we were after: $1$. So if there is no distinction between free variables and bound variables then we have to introduce mechanisms to avoid variable capture, such that $P(0,1)/(t) = P(0,t)$ rather than $P(t,1)$. However, since we do distinguish between free and bound variables from the outset there is no need for such a mechanism and the substitution function can be safely defined as in Definition \ref{def:BF-Substitution} clause 5: $\forall P(\&0,\#0)/(t) = \forall (P(\&0,\#0)/(t)) = \forall P(\&0,t)$. This makes for a more elegant notion of free-variable substitution.
nodes.statement_short: Because free and bound variables are distinguished, substitution under $\forall$ needs no capture-avoidance, unlike standard De Bruijn substitution.

nodes.name: Negation
nodes.statement: For some set of first-order BoundedFormulas $\mathcal{B}$ we define the negation operation $\neg : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}$ by $\neg(\varphi) = \varphi \rightarrow \bot$.
nodes.label: def:FO-Neg

nodes.name: Exists
nodes.statement: For some set of first-order BoundedFormulas $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,(n+1))$ we define the exists operation $\exists : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,(n + 1)) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,n)$ by $\exists(\varphi) = \neg \forall \neg \varphi$.
nodes.label: def:FO-Ex

nodes.name: Top
nodes.statement: We define $\top = \neg \bot$.
nodes.label: def:Top

nodes.name: And
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{B}$ some set of BoundedFormulas we define the function $\wedge : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}$ by $\varphi \wedge \psi = \neg (\varphi \supset \neg \psi)$.
nodes.label: def:FO-And

nodes.name: Or
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{B}$ some set of BoundedFormulas we define the function $\vee : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}$ by $\varphi \vee \psi = \neg \phi \supset \psi$.
nodes.label: def:FO-Or

nodes.name: If and Only If
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{B}$ some set of BoundedFormulas we define the function $\leftrightarrow : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}$ by $\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi = (\varphi \to \psi) \wedge (\psi \to \varphi)$.
nodes.label: def:FO-Iff

nodes.name: First-order Formula
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a first-order language and $\alpha$ a set indexing variables. Then the set of formulas with respect to $\mathcal{L}$ and $\alpha$ denoted $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\alpha)$ is defined as the set of bounded formulas $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\alpha,0)$.
also_stated_at: Formulas and sentences can conveniently be defined as a \texttt{BoundedFormula} with all its bound variables bound and a \texttt{BoundedFormula} that is a formula and does not contain free variables respectively.
nodes.label: def:FO-Formula

nodes.name: First-order Sentence
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a first-order language. Then the set of sentences with respect to $\mathcal{L}$ denoted $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{L})$ is defined as the set of formulas $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\emptyset)$.
also_stated_at: A \texttt{Sentence} is then defined as a \texttt{Formula} that has no free variables.
nodes.label: def:FO-Sentence

nodes.name: termToNat (terms with free variables)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L} = \langle (F_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}, (R_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \rangle$ be a first-order language and let $n$ be a natural number. Assume furthermore that for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$ all $f \in F_i$ have a unique associated natural number. Then the encoding function $\texttt{termToNat} : \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N} \cup \{1,...,n\}) \to \mathbb{N}$ is defined as \begin{align*} \texttt{termToNat}(t) = \texttt{Encodable.encodeList}(\texttt{Term.listEncode}(t)). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Encode terms with natural-number free variables as naturals via mathlib's list encodings.
nodes.label: def:FV-Term-Enc

nodes.name: termToNat (terms from sentences)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L} = \langle (F_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}, (R_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \rangle$ be a first-order language and let $n$ be a natural number. Assume furthermore that for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$ all $f \in F_i$ have a unique associated natural number. Then the encoding function $\texttt{termToNat} : \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},Empty \cup \{1,...,n\}) \to \mathbb{N}$ is defined as \begin{align*} \texttt{termToNat}(t) = \texttt{Encodable.encodeList}(\texttt{Term.listEncode}(t)). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Encode terms with no free variables as naturals via mathlib's list encodings.
nodes.label: def:S-Term-Enc

nodes.name: formulaToNat
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L} = \langle (F_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}, (R_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \rangle$ be a first-order language and let $n$ be a natural number. Assume furthermore that for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$ all $f \in F_i$ have a unique associated natural number and that for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$ all $r \in R_i$ have a unique associated natural number. Then the encoding function $\texttt{formulaToNat} : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N},n) \to \mathbb{N}$ is defined as \begin{align*} \texttt{formulaToNat}(\varphi) = \texttt{Encodable.encodeList}(\texttt{BoundedFormula.listEncode}(\varphi)). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Encode bounded formulas as natural numbers via mathlib's list encodings.
nodes.label: def:FV-Formula-to-N

nodes.name: sentToNat
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L} = \langle (F_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}, (R_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \rangle$ be a first-order language and let $n$ be a natural number. Assume furthermore that for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$ all $f \in F_i$ have a unique associated natural number and that for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$ all $r \in R_i$ have a unique associated natural number. Then the encoding function $\texttt{sentToNat} : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},Empty,0) \to \mathbb{N}$ is defined as \begin{align*} \texttt{sentToNat}(\varphi) = \texttt{Encodable.encodeList}(\texttt{BoundedFormula.listEncode}(\varphi)). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Encode sentences as natural numbers via mathlib's list encodings.
nodes.label: def:S-To-N

nodes.name: Function symbols of the language of Peano Arithmetic
nodes.statement: We define $(F_{\mathcal{L},i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ by \begin{enumerate} \item $(F_{\mathcal{L},0}) = \{\texttt{null}\}$, \item $(F_{\mathcal{L},1}) = \{S, \underdot{\neg} , \underdot{\forall}, \underdot{\exists}, {^\circ}\}$, \item $(F_{\mathcal{L},2}) = \{+,\times, \underdot{\wedge}, \underdot{\vee}, \underdot{\supset}\}$ and \item $(F_{\mathcal{L},3}) = \{\underdot{subs}\}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Function symbols: null; successor and dotted syntactic unary operators; +, times and dotted binary connectives; dotted subs.
nodes.label: def:L-Func

nodes.name: Relation symbols of the language of Peano Arithmetic
nodes.statement: We define $(R_{\mathcal{L},i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ by \[R_1 = \{Variable, Constant, ClosedTerm, Term, Formula_{\mathcal{L}}, Sentence_{\mathcal{L}}, \\ Formula_{\mathcal{L}_T}, Sentence_{\mathcal{L}_T}\}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Unary syntactic predicates: Variable, Constant, ClosedTerm, Term, Formula and Sentence predicates.
nodes.label: def:L-Rel

nodes.name: Language of Peano Arithmetic L
nodes.statement: The language of Peano arithmetic including syntactic functions and predicates is the first-order language $\mathcal{L} = \langle (F_{\mathcal{L},i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}, (R_{\mathcal{L},i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \rangle$.
nodes.label: def:L

nodes.name: Function symbols of L_T
nodes.statement: We define $(F_{\mathcal{L}_T,i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ by \begin{enumerate} \item $(F_{\mathcal{L},0}) = \{\texttt{null}\}$, \item $(F_{\mathcal{L},1}) = \{S, \underdot{\neg} , \underdot{\forall}, \underdot{\exists}, {^\circ}\}$, \item $(F_{\mathcal{L},2}) = \{+,\times, \underdot{\wedge}, \underdot{\vee}, \underdot{\supset}\}$ and \item $(F_{\mathcal{L},3}) = \{\underdot{subs}\}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Function symbols of $\mathcal{L}_T$, identical to those of $\mathcal{L}$.
nodes.label: def:L_T-Func

nodes.name: Relation symbols of L_T
nodes.statement: We define $(R_{\mathcal{L}_T,i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ by \[R_1 = \{Tr,Variable, Constant, ClosedTerm, Term, Formula_{\mathcal{L}}, Sentence_{\mathcal{L}}, Formula_{\mathcal{L}_T}, Sentence_{\mathcal{L}_T}\}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Relation symbols of $\mathcal{L}$ plus the truth predicate $Tr$.
nodes.label: def:L_T-Rel

nodes.name: Language L_T of Peano Arithmetic with Tr
nodes.statement: The language of Peano arithmetic including syntactic functions and predicates is the first-order language $\mathcal{L}_T = \langle (F_{\mathcal{L}_T,i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}, (R_{\mathcal{L}_T,i})_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \rangle$.
also_stated_at: We define the language of $\mathcal{L}_T$ as the language $\mathcal{L}$ one relation symbol added: $Tr$. Hence its Function symbols are equivalent to that of $\mathcal{L}$ and the relation symbols only feature an extra $Tr$.
nodes.label: def:L_T

nodes.name: L-Numeral Function
nodes.statement: We define the numeral function $num_{\mathcal{L}} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L},\alpha)$ recursively as \begin{enumerate} \item $num_{\mathcal{L}}(0) = \texttt{null}$ \item $num_{\mathcal{L}}(n + 1) = S(num_{\mathcal{L}}(n))$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:L-Numeral

nodes.name: L_T-Numeral Function
nodes.statement: We define the numeral function $num_{\mathcal{L}_T} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{L}_T,\alpha)$ recursively as \begin{enumerate} \item $num_{\mathcal{L_T}}(0) = \texttt{null}$ \item $num_{\mathcal{L_T}}(n + 1) = S(num_{\mathcal{L_T}}(n))$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:L_T-Numeral

nodes.name: Gödel quotation (numeral of a code)
nodes.statement: We shall denote the numeral corresponding to the code of a BoundedFormula $\varphi$ or Term $t$ by $\ulcorner \varphi \urcorner$ and $\ulcorner t \urcorner$ respectively.

nodes.name: Theory
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a formal language and $S_{\mathcal{L}}$ its associated set of sentences. Then, a theory of $\mathcal{L}$ is a set of sentences $T_{\mathcal{L}}$ such that $T_{\mathcal{L}} \subseteq S_{\mathcal{L}}$.
nodes.label: def:FO-Theory

nodes.name: Syntax Axioms
nodes.statement: We have formalized syntactic axiom schemes for all syntactic operators Syntax Theory. Examples include $(\underdot{\neg} \ulcorner \varphi \urcorner = \ulcorner \neg \varphi \urcorner)$, where $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$; $(\ulcorner \varphi \urcorner \underdot{\wedge} \ulcorner \psi \urcorner) = (\ulcorner \varphi \wedge \psi \urcorner)$, where $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$; $(\ulcorner \varphi \urcorner \underdot{\vee} \ulcorner \psi \urcorner = (\ulcorner \varphi \wedge \psi \urcorner)$, where $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$ and $(\ulcorner \varphi \urcorner) \underdot{\supset} \ulcorner \psi \urcorner) = (\ulcorner \phi \supset \psi)$, where $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$.
nodes.statement_short: Axiom schemes stating that the dotted syntactic operators act on codes as the connectives act on formulas.
nodes.label: def:Syntax-Axioms

nodes.name: Syntax Theory
nodes.statement: We define Syntax Theory as the theory containg all the instances of the axiom schemas for $\underdot{\neg}$, $\underdot{\wedge}$, $\underdot{\vee}$, $\underdot{\supset}$, etc.
nodes.label: def:Syntax-Theory

nodes.name: The First 6 Axioms of Peano Arithmetic
nodes.statement: The theory of the first 6 axioms of Peano Arithmetic \texttt{PA-axioms} is defined as the smallest theory $X$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\forall \neg (\&0 = S(\&0) \in X$, \item $\forall \forall (S(\&1) = S(\&0) \rightarrow \&1 = \&0) \in X$, \item $\forall (\&0 + \texttt{null} = \&0) \in X$, \item $\forall \forall (\&1 + S(\&0) = S(\&1 + \&0)) \in X$, \item $\forall (\&1 \cdot \texttt{null} = \texttt{null}) \in X$ and \item $\forall \forall (\&1 \cdot S(\&0) = \&1 \cdot \&0 + \&1) \in X$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Successor injectivity and non-fixpoint, and the recursive equations of addition and multiplication.
nodes.label: def:PA-Axioms

nodes.name: PA: The Theory of Peano Arithmetic
nodes.statement: We define \texttt{PA} as the theory $\texttt{PA-axioms} \cup \{φ | ∃ψ \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},{0}) : φ = ([ψ(\texttt{null}) \wedge ∀\langle ψ(\&0) \supset ψ(S(\&0)) \rangle ] \supset ∀ψ(\&0))\}$.
nodes.statement_short: PA = the six axioms plus all induction instances for $\mathcal{L}$-formulas.
also_stated_at: Then we define \texttt{PA} as the union of the first 6 Peano axioms and all the instances of the induction scheme for \texttt{PA}.
nodes.label: def:PA

nodes.name: PAT
nodes.statement: We define \texttt{PAT} as the theory $\texttt{PA-axioms} \cup \{φ | ∃ψ \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L}_T,{0}) : φ = ([ψ(\texttt{null}) \wedge ∀\langle ψ(\&0) \supset ψ(S(\&0)) \rangle ] \supset ∀ψ(\&0))\}$.
nodes.statement_short: PAT = the six axioms plus induction for all $\mathcal{L}_T$-formulas.
nodes.label: def:PAT

nodes.name: TB
nodes.statement: We define \texttt{TB} as $\texttt{PAT} \cup \{φ | ∃ψ \in \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{L}) : φ = T(⌜ψ⌝) \leftrightarrow ψ\}$.
nodes.statement_short: TB = PAT plus the Tarski biconditionals $T(\ulcorner\psi\urcorner)\leftrightarrow\psi$ for $\mathcal{L}$-sentences.
nodes.label: def:TB

nodes.name: Sequent Calculus (G3cp + G3c with theoretical axiom)
nodes.statement_short: Classical sequent calculus G3cp+G3c with an extra axiom introducing theory sentences in the succedent.
nodes.label: def:Seq-Calc

nodes.name: Set of All Derivations
nodes.statement: Let $Th$ be some theory in some language $\mathcal{L}$, and $\Gamma, \Delta$ finite sets such that $\Gamma, \Delta \subseteq \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$. Then we denote the set of all trees that consists only of rules from the Sequent Calculus (Definition \ref{def:Seq-Calc}) with $Th$ as theory and have as root $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$ by $\mathcal{D}(Th,\Gamma,\Delta)$.
nodes.label: def:Derivation

nodes.name: Sequent Provable from Theory
nodes.statement: We call a sequent $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$ provable from some theory $Th$, denoted $Th \vdash \Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, if there exists some derivation $d \in \mathcal{D}(Th,\Gamma,\Delta)$.
nodes.label: def:Sequent-Provable

nodes.name: Formula Provable from Theory
nodes.statement: We call a formula $\varphi$ provable from some theory $Th$, denoted $Th \vdash \varphi$, if there exists some derivation $d \in \mathcal{D}(Th,\emptyset,\{\varphi\})$.
nodes.label: def:Formula-Provable

nodes.name: MetaRules
nodes.statement: We define many meta rules which should be proved for the sequent calculus, including \begin{multicols}{2} \[ \frac{\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta}{\Gamma, A \Rightarrow \Delta} \tag{$L_{wk}$} \] \[ \frac{\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta}{\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta, A} \tag{$R_{wk}$} \] \[ \frac{}{\Gamma \Rightarrow (t_1 = t_1), \Delta} \tag{$R=$} \] \[ \frac{\Gamma \Rightarrow A \supset B, \Delta \quad \Gamma \Rightarrow B \supset A, \Delta}{\Gamma \Rightarrow A \leftrightarrow B, \Delta} \tag{$R\leftrightarrow$} \] \[ \frac{\Gamma \Rightarrow A \leftrightarrow B, \Delta}{\Gamma \Rightarrow A \supset B, \Delta} \tag{$R \leftrightarrow elim\_to\_right$} \] \[ \frac{\Gamma \Rightarrow A \leftrightarrow B, \Delta}{\Gamma \Rightarrow B \supset A, \Delta} \tag{$R \leftrightarrow elim\_to\_left$} \] \end{multicols}
nodes.statement_short: Admissible meta rules to be proved: left/right weakening, reflexivity of equality, biconditional introduction and elimination.
nodes.label: def:MetaRules

nodes.name: T-Replacement
nodes.statement: Let $n$ be some natural number. We then define the T-replacement function, for replacing all T-predicate by a some $\mathcal{L}$ formula, with respect to $n$, $TrReplace_n : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N},n) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L}_T,\mathbb{N},n) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N},n)$ recursively as \begin{enumerate} \item $TrReplace_n(\varphi,\bot) = \bot$ \item $TrReplace_n(\varphi,(t_1 = t_2)) = (t_1 = t_2)$ \item $TrReplace_n(\varphi,Tr(t)) = \varphi(t)$ \item $TrReplace_n(\varphi,(\psi_1 \supset \psi_2)) = (TrReplace_n(\varphi,\psi_1) \supset TrReplace_n(\varphi,\psi_2))$ \item $TrReplace_n(\varphi,\forall(\psi)) = \forall(TrReplace_{n + 1}(\varphi,\psi))$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Recursively replace every $Tr(t)$ in an $\mathcal{L}_T$ formula by $\varphi(t)$, yielding an $\mathcal{L}$ formula.
nodes.label: def:T-Replacement

nodes.name: T-Replacement over Set
nodes.statement: We define T-Replacement for all formulas in some set $S \subseteq \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L_T},\mathbb{N})$ as T-Replacement in all formulas $\varphi \in S$.
nodes.label: def:T-Replacement-Set

nodes.name: List
nodes.statement: We define the set of lists with respect to some set $S$, denoted $L_S$, as the smallest set $X$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $[] \in X$ and \item if $h \in S$ and $T \in X$, then $[h,T] \in X$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:List

nodes.name: List Append
nodes.statement: We define the append function for lists $\texttt{++}: L \to L \to L$ recursively by \begin{enumerate} \item $[] ~\texttt{++}~ l = l$ and \item $[h,T] ~\texttt{++}~ l = [h,T ~\texttt{++}~ L]$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:List-Append

nodes.name: Membership relation for Lists
nodes.statement: We define the membership relation for lists $\underline{\texttt{in}}$ recursively as the smallest set $X$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $(a,[a,[]]) \in X$ and \item $(a,[h,T]) \in X$ if $a = h$ or $(a,T) \in X$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:List-Mem

nodes.name: dedup: Remove Duplicates From List
nodes.statement: We define the function removing elements from a list $\texttt{dedup} : L \to L$ recursively by \begin{enumerate} \item $\texttt{dedup}([]) = []$ and \item $\texttt{dedup}([h,T]) = \begin{cases} [h,\texttt{dedup}(T)] & \text{if } \neg h ~\underline{\texttt{in}}~ T \\ \texttt{dedup}(T) & \text{if } h ~\underline{\texttt{in}}~ T \end{cases}$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:List-Dedup

nodes.name: List of Disquoted Sentences of a Derivation (with duplicates)
nodes.statement: We define the function $pre\varphi L(d) : \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\Gamma,\Delta) \to L(\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\{0\}))$ recursively by \begin{enumerate} \item $pre\varphi L(\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta, A) = \begin{cases} [\psi] & \text{if } A = Tr(\ulcorner \psi \urcorner) \leftrightarrow \psi \wedge \psi \in \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{L}) \\ \text{[]} & \text{else} \end{cases}$; \item $pre\varphi L(\frac{d}{\Gamma, \Delta}) = pre\varphi L(d)$ and \item $pre\varphi L(\frac{d_1 \quad d_2}{\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta}) = pre\varphi L(d_1) ~\texttt{++}~ pre\varphi L(d_2) $. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Collect, recursively over a TB derivation, the sentences $\psi$ whose Tarski biconditional is used as an axiom.
nodes.label: def:Pre-Rel-Phis

nodes.name: List of Disquoted Sentences of a Derivation (without duplicates)
nodes.statement: We define $\varphi L(d) : \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\Gamma,\Delta) \to L(\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\{0\}))$ by $\varphi L(d) = \texttt{dedup}(pre\varphi L(d))$.
nodes.label: def:Rel-Phis

nodes.name: TB restricted to a derivation
nodes.statement: We define restricted \texttt{TB} with respect to a specific derivation $d \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\Gamma,\Delta)$, where $\Gamma, \Delta \subseteq \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L}_{T},\mathbb{N})$, denoted \texttt{TB}$(d)$, as $\texttt{PAT} \cup \{φ | ∃ψ \in \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{L}) : φ = T(⌜ψ⌝) \leftrightarrow ψ \wedge \psi \in \varphi L(d)\}$.
nodes.statement_short: PAT plus only those Tarski biconditionals whose sentences occur in derivation $d$.
nodes.label: def:Restricted-TB

nodes.name: Halbach's tau
nodes.statement: We define $\tau : L_{\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{L})} \to \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$ by \begin{enumerate} \item $\tau([]) = \bot$ and \item $\tau([\varphi,T]) = ((\#0 = \ulcorner \varphi \urcorner) \wedge \varphi) \vee (\tau(T))$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: From a list of sentences build the $\mathcal{L}$-formula $\tau(x)$: disjunction of $x=\ulcorner\varphi\urcorner\wedge\varphi$ over the list.
nodes.label: def:Tau

nodes.name: Injectivity of formulaToNat
nodes.statement: For all formulas $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$ we have that if $\varphi \neq \psi$, then $\texttt{formulaToNat}(\varphi) \neq \texttt{formulaToNat}(\psi)$.
nodes.label: lem:Injective-ToNat

nodes.name: paPlusDerGeneral
nodes.statement: For all derivations $d_1 \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\Gamma,\Delta)$, where $\Gamma, \Delta \subseteq \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$, we define the derivation $\texttt{paPlusDerGeneral}(d_1) \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB}(d)/_{ts}(\tau(\varphi L(d))),\Gamma/_{ts}(\tau(\varphi L(d))),\Delta/_{ts}(\tau(\varphi L(d))))$ recursively as [not yet formalized].
nodes.statement_short: Map a TB derivation to a derivation from T-replaced TB(d), T-replacing by $\tau(\varphi L(d))$ throughout (not yet formalized).
nodes.label: def:PA-Plus-Der-General

nodes.name: tau-equivalences: T-Replacement in TB(d) gives PA plus tau-equivalences
nodes.statement: For all $d_1 \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\emptyset,\{\varphi\})$, where $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$, we have that $\texttt{TB}(d)/_{ts}(\tau(\varphi L(d))) = \texttt{PA} \cup \{ \tau(\varphi L(d))(\ulcorner \psi \urcorner) \leftrightarrow \psi : \psi \in \varphi L(d) \}$.
nodes.statement_short: T-replacing by $\tau$ in TB(d) yields PA plus the $\tau$-biconditionals for the sentences used in $d$.
nodes.label: lem:Tau-Equivalences

nodes.name: paPlusDer
nodes.statement: We define the function \texttt{paPlusDer}$: \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\emptyset,\{\varphi\}) \to \mathcal{D}(\texttt{PA} \cup \{ \tau(\varphi L(d))(\ulcorner \psi \urcorner) \leftrightarrow \psi : \psi \in \varphi L(d) \}, \emptyset, \{\varphi \})$, for some $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$ by \texttt{paPlusDer}$(d) = \texttt{paPlusDerGeneral}(d)$. That the resulting derivation is in the co-domain can be obtained from Definition \ref{def:PA-Plus-Der-General}, Lemma \ref{lem:Tau-Equivalences} and the fact that $\emptyset/_{ts}(\varphi) = \emptyset$ for any $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$ and $\{\psi\}/_{ts}(\varphi) = \{\psi\}$ for any $\psi, \varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$.
nodes.statement_short: Map TB derivations of $\varphi$ to derivations of $\varphi$ from PA plus $\tau$-equivalences, via paPlusDerGeneral.
nodes.label: def:PA-Plus-Der

nodes.name: paProvesAllTauDisq
nodes.statement: Let $[h,T] \in L_{\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{L})}$ and $\varphi ~\underline{\texttt{in}}~ [h,T]$. Then the partial function $\texttt{paProvesAllTauDisq}: L_{\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{L})} \times \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{L}) \rightharpoonup \mathcal{D}(\texttt{PA},\Gamma,\Delta \cup \{\tau([h,T])(\ulcorner \psi \urcorner) \leftrightarrow \psi \})$ is (with a slight abuse of notation) defined by $\texttt{paProvesAllTauDisq}([h,T],\varphi) = \begin{cases} \href{https://github.com/ppls-nd-prs/formalizing-axiomatic-theories-of-truth/blob/main/blueprint/src/img/h-is-psi.pdf}{\text{h-is-psi.pdf}} & \text{if } h = \psi \\ \href{https://github.com/ppls-nd-prs/formalizing-axiomatic-theories-of-truth/blob/main/blueprint/src/img/h-is-not-psi.pdf}{\text{h-is-not-psi.pdf}} & \text{otherwise } \end{cases}$. The derivations themselves are linked as they are rather large.
nodes.statement_short: Partial function giving PA derivations of each $\tau$-biconditional, by cases on whether the list head is $\psi$.
nodes.label: def:PA-Proves-All-Tau-Disq

nodes.name: paPlusToPa
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$, and $d \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\emptyset,\{\varphi\})$. Then we define the function \texttt{paPlusToPa}$: \mathcal{D}(\texttt{PA} \cup \{\tau(\varphi L(d))(\ulcorner \psi \urcorner) \leftrightarrow \psi : \psi \in \varphi L(d)\},\Gamma,\Delta) \to \mathcal{D}(\texttt{PA},\Gamma,\Delta)$ by \begin{enumerate} \item $\texttt{paPlusToPa}(\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta, A) = \begin{cases} \Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta, A & \text{if } A \in \texttt{PA} \\ \texttt{paProvesAllTauDisq}(\varphi L(d),A) & \text{else} \end{cases}$; \item $\texttt{paPlusToPa}(\frac{d}{\Gamma, \Delta}) = \frac{\texttt{paPlusToPa}(d)}{\Gamma, \Delta}$ and \item $\texttt{paPlusToPa}(\frac{d_1 \quad d_2}{\Gamma, \Delta}) = \frac{\texttt{paPlusToPa}(d_1) \quad \texttt{paPlusToPa}(d_2)}{\Gamma, \Delta}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Turn derivations from PA plus $\tau$-equivalences into PA derivations by replacing each $\tau$-axiom leaf with its PA derivation.
nodes.label: def:PA-Plus-To-PA

nodes.name: Translation
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi$ be a formula $\varphi \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$. Then we define the translation function with respect to that formula $\texttt{translation}_{\varphi} : \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\emptyset,\{\varphi\}) \to \mathcal{D}(\texttt{PA},\emptyset,\{\varphi\})$ as $\texttt{translation}_{\varphi}(d) = \texttt{paPlusToPa}(\texttt{paPlusDer}(d))$.
nodes.statement_short: Translation of TB derivations of $\varphi$ into PA derivations: paPlusToPa after paPlusDer.
nodes.label: def:Translation

nodes.name: Conservativity of TB over PA
nodes.statement: $\forall \varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N}) : \texttt{TB} \vdash \varphi \Rightarrow \texttt{PA} \vdash \varphi$
nodes.statement_short: Every $\mathcal{L}$-formula provable in TB is provable in PA.
nodes.label: def:ConservativityTB

nodes.name: Proof of Conservativity of TB over PA
nodes.statement: Let $\psi$ be an arbitrary formula such that $\psi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$ and assume $\psi$ is provable from \texttt{TB}. Then, by Definition \ref{def:Formula-Provable}, there exists some derivation $d \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\emptyset,\{\psi\})$. Then, by Definition \ref{def:Translation}, we have $\texttt{translation}(d) \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{PA},\emptyset,\{\psi\})$. Then, by Definition \ref{def:Formula-Provable}, we have that $\psi$ is provable from \texttt{PA}. Then, as we assumed that $\psi$ is provable from \texttt{TB}, we have that if $\texttt{TB} \vdash \psi$, then $\texttt{PA} \vdash \psi$. And since $\psi$ was arbitrary we have that for all $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L}, \mathbb{N})$ if $\texttt{TB} \vdash \varphi$, then $\texttt{PA} \vdash \varphi$.
nodes.statement_short: Direct: take a TB derivation of $\psi$ and apply the translation function to obtain a PA derivation.

nodes.name: Assume TB proves psi; obtain derivation
nodes.statement: Let $\psi$ be an arbitrary formula such that $\psi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L},\mathbb{N})$ and assume $\psi$ is provable from \texttt{TB}. Then, by Definition \ref{def:Formula-Provable}, there exists some derivation $d \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{TB},\emptyset,\{\psi\})$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix arbitrary $\psi$ provable in TB and take a TB derivation $d$

nodes.name: Apply the translation
nodes.statement: Then, by Definition \ref{def:Translation}, we have $\texttt{translation}(d) \in \mathcal{D}(\texttt{PA},\emptyset,\{\psi\})$.
nodes.statement_short: Translate $d$ into a PA derivation

nodes.name: Conclude PA proves psi
nodes.statement: Then, by Definition \ref{def:Formula-Provable}, we have that $\psi$ is provable from \texttt{PA}.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold provability: PA proves $\psi$

nodes.name: Generalize
nodes.statement: Then, as we assumed that $\psi$ is provable from \texttt{TB}, we have that if $\texttt{TB} \vdash \psi$, then $\texttt{PA} \vdash \psi$. And since $\psi$ was arbitrary we have that for all $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L}, \mathbb{N})$ if $\texttt{TB} \vdash \varphi$, then $\texttt{PA} \vdash \varphi$.
nodes.statement_short: Discharge assumption and generalize over $\psi$
